title: Segment
description: One story cut out of one broadcast: what `breakingnews segments` emits and what `breakingnews merge` consumes. Rows are the analysis unit downstream; `record_id` is carried on every row so a result can always be rolled back up to the broadcast that produced it. Character spans are contiguous and gapless across a record, which is what makes the merge byte-exact.

segment_id.description: `{record_id}#{index:03d}`. Stable across re-runs as long as the number of segments in the record does not change. It deliberately encodes no offset: predicted offsets are not bit-reproducible across batch sizes (LIMITATIONS L1b), so an offset-derived or content-hashed id would churn on a re-run that found exactly the same stories. What an ordinal id does NOT survive is a re-segmentation with a different segment count, which renumbers everything after the change -- reconcile two runs on `record_id` plus `word_start`, not on this.

record_id.description: The parent broadcast, carried verbatim. Provenance never requires parsing `segment_id`.

index.description: Position within the broadcast, from 0. Contiguous: a record with N segments has indices 0..N-1 with none missing.

word_start.description: First word offset, inclusive, into `body.split()`. Segment 0 always starts at 0.

word_end.description: Last word offset, exclusive. The final segment's `word_end` equals the record's `word_count`.

char_start.description: First character offset, inclusive, into the original `body`. Segment 0 always starts at 0, so leading whitespace is not lost.

char_end.description: Last character offset, exclusive. Equals the next segment's `char_start`, and for the final segment equals `len(body)`. This gaplessness is what makes concatenation reproduce the source byte-for-byte.

text.description: The exact substring `body[char_start:char_end]`, including the whitespace separating this segment from the next -- that is what makes the merge lossless. Strip it for display or analysis. Omitted entirely when segments are built with `include_text=False`, which is how to publish segment offsets for a licensed corpus without redistributing its text; the merge is then unavailable.

flags.description: Advisory markers, never a record of removal -- segmentation drops nothing. `short` means below the caller's `--min-words`; `empty` means zero words. Discarding flagged rows is an explicit, separate step (`drop_flagged`), and once rows are dropped the remainder is no longer a gapless cover, so the merge will refuse it.

outlet.description: Passed through from the transcript, if present.

show.description: Passed through from the transcript, if present.

date.description: Passed through from the transcript, if present.
